response.text:
What the white whale was to Ahab has been hinted; what, at times, he was to me remains unsaid. Aside from those more obvious considerations, there was another thought, or rather vague, nameless horror concerning him, which at times by its intensity completely overpowered all the rest; and yet so mystical and well nigh ineffable was it, that I almost despair of putting it in a comprehensible form. It was the whiteness of the whale that above all things appalled me. But how can I hope to explain myself here; and yet, in some dim, random way, explain myself I must, else all these chapters might be naught. Though in many things whiteness refiningly enhances—marbles, japonicas, pearls; banners and chargers; the ermine and the alb of priests; the white belt of wampum; the Persian white flame, and in the Vision of St. John white robes, a great white throne, the Holy One white like wool; and though this pre-eminence in it applies to the human race itself, giving the white man ideal mastership over every dusky tribe; yet for all these accumulated associations, there lurks an elusive something in the innermost idea of this hue that strikes more of panic to the soul than the redness of blood.

Divorced from kindly associations and coupled with what is terrible, whiteness heightens terror to the furthest bounds. Witness the white bear and the white shark—their ghastly whiteness imparting an abhorrent mildness to their dumb gloating. Not the heraldic tiger so staggers courage as the white-shrouded ghostliness of those pale marauders. The French, alluding to the white, silent stillness of death, call that shark Requin—from Requiem.

Bethink thee of the albatross: in its wondrous bodily whiteness chiefly lurks the spell; Not Coleridge first threw that spell; but God’s great, unflattering laureate, Nature. I remember the first I ever saw—regal, unspotted, hooked Roman bill; at intervals it arched forth its vast archangel wings as if to embrace some holy ark; wondrous flutterings shook it; though bodily unharmed it uttered cries. Through its inexpressible, strange eyes, methought I peeped to secrets which took hold of God. As Abraham before the angels, I bowed myself. “Goney!” cried a sailor; the truth was in the bird’s whiteness.

So, too, the White Steed of the Prairies—milk-white, small-headed, bluff-chested, an apparition imperial and archangelical of that unfallen, western world, which to the eyes of the old trappers and hunters revived the glories of those primeval times when Adam walked majestic as a god—whose spiritual whiteness clothed him with divineness that enforced a nameless terror. And yet there are other whitenesses that lose strange glory and acquire a repelling chill: the Albino, invested in all-pervading pallor, more hideous than deformity; the White Squall; the White Hoods of Ghent masked in their snowy faction; the marble pallor of the dead, the shroud’s hue, and ghosts rising in a milk-white fog; yea, even Death, riding his pallid horse.

Name alone can summon a spectralness: the White Tower; the White Mountains; the White Sea; “the tall pale man” of the Hartz. Nor is it earthquakes and stampedoes alone that make tearless Lima the strangest, saddest city: for Lima has taken the white veil; and there is a higher horror in this whiteness of her woe. Old as Pizarro, this whiteness keeps her ruins for ever new; admits not the cheerful greenness of complete decay; spreads over her broken ramparts the rigid pallor of an apoplexy that fixes its own distortions.

To the common apprehension this phenomenon is not prime in terror; yet often the very thing that appals is the whiteness. A mariner, called by night to view his ship sailing through a midnight sea of milky whiteness, feels a silent dread, as if shoals of combed white bears swam around him; the lead assures soundings, but heart and helm go down till blue water is under him again. The backwoodsman views with indifference a prairie sheeted with snow; but not so the sailor in Antarctic scenes, where boundless churchyards grin with icy monuments and splintered crosses.

“White-lead chapter,” sayest thou? “White flag hung out from a craven soul?” Tell me, then, why a strong colt, smelling only the musk of a buffalo robe, starts and snorts with bursting eyes though he never knew the goring bisons of Oregon. Here behold, even in a brute, the instinct of the demonism in the world. So to me the milky sea, the frost-festoons, the windrowed snows—are the shaken robe to the frightened colt.

Though neither knows where lie the nameless things of which the mystic sign gives forth such hints; yet with me, as with the colt, somewhere those things must exist. Though in many of its aspects this visible world seems formed in love, the invisible spheres were formed in fright.

But not yet the incantation is solved. Why should that which is emblem of the Christian’s Deity be also intensifier of the appalling? Is it that by its indefiniteness it shadows forth the heartless voids and immensities of the universe, stabbing us with annihilation at the sight of the milky way? Or that whiteness is not so much a colour as the visible absence of colour; and at the same time the concrete of all colours; is it for these reasons that there is such a dumb blankness, full of meaning, in a wide landscape of snows—a colourless, all-colour of atheism from which we shrink? And when we remember the philosophers who tell us all earthly hues—sunset tinges, butterfly cheeks—are but subtile deceits laid on from without; that all deified Nature absolutely paints like the harlot, whose allurements cover nothing but the charnel-house within; and that the mystical cosmetic that produces every hue—Light itself—for ever remains white; and that, operating unmediated, it would touch even roses with its own blank tinge—pondering all this, the palsied universe lies before us a leper; and like travellers in Lapland refusing coloured glasses, the infidel gazes himself blind at the monumental white shroud that wraps all the prospect round him. And of all these things the Albino whale was the symbol. Wonder ye then at the fiery hunt?
